per_case.answer:
Treat apple scab by combining cultural controls with fungicide applications.  
Plant scab‑resistant cultivars such as ‘Goldrush’, ‘Enterprise’, ‘Pristine’, ‘Gala Supreme’, ‘Liberty’, ‘Freedom’ or ‘Jonafree’, and clean up fallen leaves each season to reduce inoculum [1].  

For active infections, spray either an organic or a conventional product. Organic options include sulfur 80 % WDG, potassium bicarbonate, or the biocontrol Bacillus subtilis [3]. Conventional chemicals are Captan 50 % WP (2.5 g per litre of spray mix) or Difenoconazole 25 % EC (0.5 ml per litre) applied at 7–10 day intervals, with a 14‑day pre‑harvest interval and full PPE protection [3][4].

per_case.answer: The disease is managed by suppressing the Asian citrus psyllid and supporting tree nutrition. Typical programs use systemic neonicotinoids such as imidacloprid (17.8 % SL) or thiamethoxam (25 % WG) applied as a soil drench or foliar spray at 0.5 ml/L (imidacloprid) or 0.3 g/L (thiamethoxam) on a 21‑30‑day interval, combined with horticultural mineral oil (1‑2 %) and kaolin‑clay barriers to deter oviposition, and the release of the parasitoid Tamarixia radiata as a biological control [3][4]. Additional vector‑control options include rotating foliar insecticides such as dimethoate, chlorpyrifos, zeta‑cypermethrin, bifenthrin or spirotetramat, and applying frequent foliar micronutrient sprays (Zn, Mn, Fe, etc.) to improve tree health [5].
